'''Mohindar Singh Seehra''' (born 1940) is an Indian-American Physicist, academic and researcher. He is Eberly Distinguished Professor Emeritus at [[West Virginia University]] (WVU).<ref name=WVU>{{cite web|url=https://physics.wvu.edu/news-and-events/department-news/2017/01/20/professor-mohindar-singh-seehra-retires|title=Professor Mohindar Singh Seehra Retires|date=20 January 2017 }}</ref>

Seehra has authored over 325 publications. His research has focused on structural and magnetic properties of materials, with focus on nanomaterials and thin films, and their applications in catalysis and biomedicine. He is a fellow of the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]], [[American Physical Society]] (APS),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=2020&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive}}</ref> and [[Institute of Physics]] (UK). WVU has honored him with the Buswell Award for advancing the career of women scientists under his mentorship and Order of Vandalia Award for Distinguished Service.<ref name=WVU/>

Seehra has edited books on  Magnetic Spinels, Nanostructured Materials, and Noble and Precious Metals, published by InTech Publishers (UK).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=7RffgSEAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Mohinder Seehra - Google Scholar}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Seehra was born in 1940 in a village near the town of [[Burewala]] which is now part of [[Pakistan]]. During the independence and partition of British India in 1947, he along with his family migrated to India and received his early education there.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiaabroad.com/india/from-partition-of-the-indian-subcontinent-a-hard-won-wholeness/article_0b4b2aa8-6cb8-11e7-a438-f7751e025b91.html|title=From Partition of the Indian Subcontinent, a hard-won wholeness|access-date=2021-03-26|archive-date=2020-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109040813/https://www.indiaabroad.com/india/from-partition-of-the-indian-subcontinent-a-hard-won-wholeness/article_0b4b2aa8-6cb8-11e7-a438-f7751e025b91.html}}</ref> He graduated from high school in 1955, followed by B.Sc. degree in 1959 from R.K. Arya College of Punjab University. He then worked as a Laboratory Instructor in Chemistry at the Arya College for one year. In 1960, he enrolled in [[Aligarh University]] and received his M.Sc. degree in Physics in 1962, followed by one-year teaching as a Lecturer in Physics at Jain College, Ambala City. In 1963, he moved to the [[United States]], earning his Ph.D. in Physics from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1969.<ref name=WVU/>

==Career==
After receiving Ph.D. in 1969, Seehra joined West Virginia University (WVU) as [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] of Physics, becoming Associate Professor in 1973 and full Professor in 1977. In 1992, he was appointed Eberly Family Distinguished Professor of Physics. After retiring in 2016 as Eberly Distinguished Professor Emeritus at WVU, he continues collaborative research with research groups in USA and India.<ref name=WVU/>

==Research==
Broadly, Seehra's research work has focused on structural and magnetic properties of [[transition metal]] oxides, sulfides, fluorides, spinels, perovskites and carbons, and size and surface effects in magnetic nanostructures and their applications in catalysis and biomedicine.

===Magnetic nanoparticles===
Seehra's work includes that on [[Copper(II) oxide|CuO]] nanoparticles (NPs)  which  showed strong size and temperature dependence of magnetism in CuO NPs prepared by the sol-gel method and structural characterization via x-ray diffraction and [[high-resolution transmission electron microscopy]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.64.174420|title=Bulk to nanoscale magnetism and exchange bias in CuO nanoparticles|year=2001|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.64.174420|last1=Punnoose|first1=A.|last2=Magnone|first2=H.|last3=Seehra|first3=M. S.|last4=Bonevich|first4=J.|journal=Physical Review B|volume=64|issue=17|article-number=174420 |bibcode=2001PhRvB..64q4420P |url-access=subscription}}</ref> For [[Cerium(IV) oxide|CeO<sub>2</sub>]] NPs with applications in biomedicine and catalysis, his research implied that transformation of Ce<sup>4+</sup> to Ce<sup>3+</sup> driven by oxygen vacancies is the key factor to understand the catalytic properties of ceria.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cm061580n|title= Concentration of Ce3+ and Oxygen Vacancies in Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles|year= 2006|doi= 10.1021/cm061580n|last1= Dutta|first1= P.|last2= Pal|first2= S.|last3= Seehra|first3= M. S.|last4= Shi|first4= Y.|last5= Eyring|first5= E. M.|last6= Ernst|first6= R. D.|journal= Chemistry of Materials|volume= 18|issue= 21|pages= 5144–5146|url-access= subscription}}</ref> Another important research has been the ferromagnetic and semiconducting behavior of sputtered Co-doped [[Titanium dioxide|TiO<sub>2</sub>]] thin films above room temperature.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1452650|title=Semiconducting and ferromagnetic behavior of sputtered Co-doped TiO2 thin films above room temperature|journal=Journal of Applied Physics |year=2002 |volume=91 |issue=10 |page=8093 |doi=10.1063/1.1452650|last1=Park |first1=Wan Kyu |last2=Ortega-Hertogs |first2=Ricardo J. |last3=Moodera |first3=Jagadeesh S. |last4=Punnoose |first4=Alex |last5=Seehra |first5=M. S. |bibcode=2002JAP....91.8093P |url-access=subscription }}</ref> For [[Cobalt(II,III) oxide|Co<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>]] NPs, he used magnetic and electron magnetic resonance studies and showed how the properties of NPs differ from those of bulk Co<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0953-8984/20/01/015218|title=A comparative study of the magnetic properties of bulk and nanocrystalline Co3O4|year=2008|doi=10.1088/0953-8984/20/01/015218|last1=Dutta|first1=P.|last2=Seehra|first2=M. S.|last3=Thota|first3=S.|last4=Kumar|first4=J.|journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter|volume=20|issue=1 |article-number=015218|bibcode=2008JPCM...20a5218D |s2cid=55609724 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Among his other notable magnetic studies on NPs are those on nearly defect-free maghemite NPs,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.70.174428|title=Magnetic properties of nearly defect-free maghemite nanocrystals|year=2004|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.70.174428|last1=Dutta|first1=P.|last2=Manivannan|first2=A.|last3=Seehra|first3=M. P.|journal=Physical Review B|volume=69|issue=5|article-number=054425 |bibcode=2004PhRvB..69e4425P }}</ref> [[Cadmium selenide|CdSe]] quantum dots,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.71.201307|title=Size-dependent properties of CdSe quantum dots|year=2005|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.71.201307|last1=Neeleshwar|first1=S.|last2=Chen|first2=C. L.|last3=Tsai|first3=C. B.|last4=Chen|first4=Y. Y.|last5=Chen|first5=C. C.|last6=Shyu|first6=S. G.|last7=Seehra|first7=M. ===Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy===
Trained in EPR spectroscopy during his Ph.D. work, Seehra discovered the sample size effect in EPR which affects the EPR linewidths,<ref>{{cite journal|title=New Method for Measuring the Static Magnetic Susceptibility by Paramagnetic Resonance|year=1968|doi=10.1063/1.1683559|last1=Seehra|first1=Mohindar S.|journal=Review of Scientific Instruments|volume=39|issue=7|pages=1044–1047|bibcode=1968RScI...39.1044S |doi-access=free}}</ref> he then went on to study various factors that affect the EPR linewidths<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.4.38|title=Antisymmetric Exchange and Exchange-Narrowed Electron-Paramagnetic-Resonance Linewidths|year=1971|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.4.38|last1=Castner|first1=T. G.|last2=Seehra|first2=Mohindar S.|journal=Physical Review B|volume=4|issue=1 |pages=38–45|bibcode=1971PhRvB...4...38C |url-access=subscription}}</ref> with special attention to the changes observed near magnetic ordering temperatures such as in antiferromagnet [[Manganese(II) fluoride|MnF<sub>2</sub>]],<ref>{{cite journal|title=Frequency Dependence of the EPR Linewidth in MnF2 Near the Critical Point|year=1971|doi=10.1063/1.1660219|last1=Seehra|first1=Mohindar S.|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=42|issue=4|pages=1290–1292|bibcode=1971JAP....42.1290S |doi-access=free}}</ref> and ferromagnets [[Chromium(III) bromide|CrBr<sub>3</sub>]]<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/pssb.2220740114|title=Electron Paramagnetic Resonance in Anisotropic Magnets|year=1976|doi=10.1002/pssb.2220740114|last1=Hùber|first1=D. L.|last2=Seehra|first2=M. S.|journal=Physica Status Solidi B|volume=74|issue=1 |pages=145–149|bibcode=1976PSSBR..74..145H |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and La<sub>0.7</sub>Sr<sub>0.3</sub>MnO<sub>3</sub>,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0953-8984/8/50/048|title=The linear temperature dependence of the paramagnetic resonance linewidth in the manganate perovskites|year=1996|doi=10.1088/0953-8984/8/50/048|last1=Seehra|first1=Mohindar S.|last2=Ibrahim|first2=Manjula M.|last3=Babu|first3=V Suresh|last4=Srinivasan|first4=G.|journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter|volume=8|issue=50|pages=11283–11289|s2cid=250872679 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and ([[Potassium perchromate|K<sub>3</sub>CrO<sub>8</sub>]]).<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.441284|title=Paramagnetic resonance, magnetic susceptibility, and antiferromagnetic exchange in a Cr5+ paramagnet: Potassium perchromate (K3CrO8)|year=1981|doi=10.1063/1.441284|last1=Dalal|first1=N. S.|last2=Millar|first2=J. M.|last3=Jagadeesh|first3=M. S.|last4=Seehra|first4=M. S.|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=74|issue=3|pages=1916–1923|bibcode=1981JChPh..74.1916D |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He also conducted a study focused on the role of magnetic anisotropy and spin-lattice coupling in the temperature dependence of EPR linewidths. His research combining theory, EPR and magnetic studies explained the origin of spin canting in [[Manganese(II,III) oxide|Mn<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260543323|title=Magnetic properties of Mn3O4 and a solution of the canted-spin problem}}</ref>

===Magnetic-Optical-Dielectric Correlations===
In his paper published in 2006, he studied structural and multiferroic properties of La-modified [[Bismuth ferrite|BiFeO<sub>3</sub>]] ceramics and showed enhancement in the multiferroic properties of BiFeO<sub>3</sub> due to stabilization of crystal structure and nonuniformity in spin cycloid structure by La substitution.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.2432869|title=Structural and multiferroic properties of La-modified BiFeO3 ceramics|year=2007|doi=10.1063/1.2432869|last1=Das|first1=S. R.|last2=Choudhary|first2=R. N. P.|last3=Bhattacharya|first3=P.|last4=Katiyar|first4=R. S.|last5=Dutta|first5=P.|last6=Manivannan|first6=A.|last7=Seehra|first7=M. S.|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=101|issue=3|pages=034104–034104–7 |bibcode=2007JAP...101c4104D |url-access=subscription}}</ref> 
Seehra investigated the temperature dependence of dielectric constants of [[Manganese(II) oxide|MnO]] and MnF<sub>2</sub><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3719/19/10/016|title=Effect of temperature and antiferromagnetic ordering on the dielectric constants of MnO and MnF2|year=1986|doi=10.1088/0022-3719/19/10/016|last1=Seehra|first1=M. S.|last2=Helmick|first2=R. E.|last3=Srinivasan|first3=G.|journal=Journal of Physics C: Solid State Physics|volume=19|issue=10|pages=1627–1635|bibcode=1986JPhC...19.1627S |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and discussed how the dielectric, magnetic and optical properties are related. In [[Nickel(II) oxide|NiO]] NPs, his studies showed how the size dependence of the magnetic ordering temperature and optical properties are related.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.4838915|title=Size-dependent shifts of the Néel temperature and optical band-gap in NiO nanoparticles|year=2013|doi=10.1063/1.4838915|last1=Thota|first1=Subhash|last2=Shim|first2=J. H.|last3=Seehra|first3=M. S.|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=114|issue=21|pages=214307–214307–4 |bibcode=2013JAP...114u4307T |url-access=subscription}}</ref> The decrease in the optical [[band gap]] of the semiconductor [[pyrite|FeS<sub>2</sub>]] with increase in temperature were compared with those in Si and Ge.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.18.7062|title=Optical absorption in iron pyrite (FeS2)|year=1978|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.18.7062|last1=Kou|first1=William W.|last2=Seehra|first2=Mohindar S.|journal=Physical Review B|volume=18|issue=12|pages=7062–7068|bibcode=1978PhRvB..18.7062K |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Carbons ===
Seehra's research on carbons include modeling of disorder in graphitic carbons,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0008622396000851|title= Modeling of disorder and X-ray diffraction in coal-based graphitic carbons
|year= 1996
|doi= 10.1016/0008-6223(96)00085-1
|last1= Babu
|first1= V.Suresh
|last2= Seehra
|first2= M.S.
|journal= Carbon
|volume= 34
|issue= 10
|pages= 1259–1265
|bibcode= 1996Carbo..34.1259B
|url-access= subscription
}}</ref> x-ray diffraction and [[Raman spectroscopy]] of commercial graphene-based materials<ref>{{cite journal|title= Correlation between X-ray diffraction and Raman spectra of 16 commercial graphene–based materials and their resulting classification|year= 2017|doi= 10.1016/j.carbon.2016.10.010|last1= Seehra|first1= Mohindar S.|last2= Narang|first2= Vishal|last3= Geddam|first3= Usha K.|last4= Stefaniak|first4= Aleksandr B.|journal= Carbon|volume= 111|pages= 380–385|pmid= 28690336|pmc= 5497829|bibcode= 2017Carbo.111..380S}}</ref> and use of nanocarbons for energy-efficient hydrogen production via water electrolysis.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S036031990900891X|title=Nanocarbon boosts energy-efficient hydrogen production in carbon-assisted water electrolysis|year=2009 |doi=10.1016/j.ijhydene.2009.06.023 |last1=Seehra |first1=M.S. |last2=Bollineni |first2=S. |journal=International Journal of Hydrogen Energy |volume=34 |issue=15 |pages=6078–6084 |bibcode=2009IJHE...34.6078S |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1973-76 - Research Fellow, Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
*1984 - Fellow, American Physical Society
*1985 - Outstanding Researcher of the College of Arts and Sciences award, West Virginia University
*1992 - Eberly Family Distinguished Professor of Physics, West Virginia University
*2001 - Fellow, Institute of Physics(UK)
*2010 - Outstanding Referee, American Physical Society (APS)<ref name=ANM>{{cite web|url=https://www.24-7pressrelease.com/press-release/444941/mohindar-singh-seehra-phd-presented-with-the-albert-nelson-marquis-lifetime-achievement-award-by-marquis-whos-who|title=Mohindar Singh Seehra, PhD, Presented with the Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award by Marquis Who's Who}}</ref>
*2015 - Mary Catherine Buswell Award, West Virginia University<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cwc.wvu.edu/awards/past-mary-catherine-buswell-award-winners|title=Past Mary Catherine Buswell Award Winners}}</ref>
*2017 - Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award, Marquis Who's Who in America<ref name=ANM/>
*2019 - Order of Vandalia Award for distinguished service to West Virginia University<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vandalia.wvu.edu/roll-of-the-order-of-vandalia|title=Roll of the Order of Vandalia}}</ref>
